events.title: US August goods-and-services trade balance
events.why_it_matters: Advance goods deficit already printed at $132.6bn (widest since the 2025 tariff surge) on oil and AI-capex imports; the 8:30 ET full report adds services and is a Q3 GDP drag read.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the overall deficit blows out with petroleum/capital-goods imports or services surplus cushions it after the US–China truce.

events.title: China Golden Week travel vs spend (final holiday days)
events.why_it_matters: Record trip volume with subdued per-trip spend is the live test of whether PBoC/mortgage support is thawing households or property-scarred consumers still travel more and spend less.
events.what_to_watch: Ministry of Culture and Tourism full-week trip/revenue print after Oct 7, plus onshore reopen tape Oct 8.

events.title: US–Iran war: Hormuz stays restricted; Iran's 7 conditions rejected
events.why_it_matters: Seven-month war plus a contested Strait of Hormuz keeps a regime-level oil, shipping, diesel, and inflation premium in global risk assets into US midterms.
events.what_to_watch: Tanker incidents, US carrier buildup, and whether Washington answers Iran's reopen conditions with strikes rather than a deal.

events.title: Brent ~$100–102 as Hormuz logistics, not just barrels, bite
events.why_it_matters: Crude transits have partially recovered via escorts/bypasses, but insurance, tanker rates, and refined-product tightness keep a consumer-tax and CPI/PPI input in place.
events.what_to_watch: Diesel/crack spreads, Hormuz AIS volumes, and any IEA/SPR or European diesel-reserve follow-through after the US diesel tax EO.

events.title: California late-season heat / wildfire-smoke risk
events.why_it_matters: Record October heat lifts power demand and fire/insurance risk into SEMICON West week — a local but tradeable utilities overlay.
events.what_to_watch: CAISO peaks, any new large-loss wildfires, and whether cooling after ~Oct 8 ends the event.

events.title: Taiwan gray-zone pressure vs silicon-shield (no invasion priced as imminent)
events.why_it_matters: Coast-guard/quarantine tactics and cable-patrol pressure are the slow-burn risk to TSMC power/shipping — a chip-supply tail, not the base case.
events.what_to_watch: Any customs-quarantine trial around outlying islands, cable cuts, or Taiwan AI-chip export-control tightening into TSMC's Oct 15 print.

events.title: Micron confirms AI-memory tightness through FY28
events.why_it_matters: Record FYQ4 and sold-out HBM into 2027 validate the Korea/Japan memory boom that ASML/TSMC/SEMICON commentary will be read against this month.
events.what_to_watch: Contract-price commentary from Samsung/SK hynix and tool-order language at SEMICON West / ASML.

events.title: September NFP miss: +29k, U3 4.2%, wages +3.0% y/y
events.why_it_matters: Payrolls badly missed ~+90k, prior months revised down, wages slowed — collapsing October FOMC hike odds to ~20% while leaving a growth-scare tail under $100 oil.
events.what_to_watch: Whether CPI (Oct 14) and retail sales (Oct 15) confirm demand destruction or just a hiring freeze.

events.title: ISM Services PMI 54.9 with prices at 74.0
events.why_it_matters: Services still expanding after the NFP miss, but the prices index at a 2022 high shows oil/war cost-push is already in the dominant sector of GDP.
events.what_to_watch: Employment subindex staying ≥50 vs CPI services/supercore on Oct 14.

events.title: Eurozone September flash HICP 3.8% y/y (energy spike)
events.why_it_matters: Hottest headline since 2023, energy 18.8% y/y, tests the ECB's post-September 25 bp hike 'hold' into the Oct 29 meeting.
events.what_to_watch: Oct 16 final HICP revisions and whether core stays near 2.5% or energy passthrough lifts services.

events.title: OPEC+ holds November output targets unchanged
events.why_it_matters: Core producers paused after finishing the 1.65 mb/d unwind; actual barrels remain far below quotas because of the Iran war, so the signal is 'no extra supply'.
events.what_to_watch: Compliance vs war-lost Iranian barrels; any emergency JMMC add if Hormuz flows collapse again.

events.title: Camp David Iran 'war council' after Hormuz rejection
events.why_it_matters: Senior US principals met with no readout as Iran restated Hormuz stays shut; raises odds of a military or sanctions step before midterms rather than a 7-day reopen deal.
events.what_to_watch: Third carrier arrival timing, any new blockade/strike order, and Trump 'easy way or hard way' decision language.

events.title: Tokyo September core CPI +2.7% y/y (hot lead for national CPI)
events.why_it_matters: Well above ~2.3% consensus after BoJ's Sept hike to 1.25%, keeping another hike in play at the Oct 29–30 meeting (just outside this window).
events.what_to_watch: National September CPI on Oct 23 as the last hard print into that meeting.

events.title: Emergency diesel excise-tax relief EO
events.why_it_matters: White House deferred diesel excise tax and dyed-diesel highway penalties through year-end — a political affordability patch that does not add barrels.
events.what_to_watch: IRS implementing guidance within 5 days, any legislative push to forgive deferred tax, and whether pump diesel actually eases.

events.title: US–China truce extended to Jan 10 plus $60bn relief lists
events.why_it_matters: Bessent/He rollover to Jan 10 2027 plus reciprocal ~$30bn-each non-sensitive lists cut the near-term China tariff cliff even as baseline duties remain.
events.what_to_watch: Implementation of the 30-for-30 lists vs any Graham Act secondary-tariff collision with China.

events.title: CIT orders extra briefs in global Section 301 forced-labor tariff case
events.why_it_matters: A three-judge CIT panel is probing whether USTR's July 24 ~10–12.5% duties on ~60 economies exceed Section 301 — a binary for stacked global tariffs.
events.what_to_watch: Supplemental briefs due Oct 16; any vacatur would be market-wide, not China-only.

events.title: Federal judge vacates FTC expanded HSR premerger rule
events.why_it_matters: E.D. Texas struck the 2024 expanded Hart-Scott-Rodino notification rule, easing deal-friction costs if the vacatur survives appeal.
events.what_to_watch: FTC appeal and whether the 7-day stay becomes a longer freeze of the old expanded form.

events.title: FCC repeals 39% national TV ownership cap
events.why_it_matters: Case-by-case review replaces the hard national audience cap, reopening broadcast consolidation optionality.
events.what_to_watch: First large-group transfer applications and any congressional/public-interest challenges.

events.title: China official manufacturing PMI back above 50 at 50.1
events.why_it_matters: Factories returned to expansion (Caixin 52.1) into Golden Week, with AI-related demand cited — a modest growth offset to weak household spend.
events.what_to_watch: Post-holiday activity and whether property/consumption still lag the factory bounce.

events.title: Brazil first-round: Flávio Bolsonaro ~47% vs Lula ~45%, runoff Oct 25
events.why_it_matters: Right-wing shock lead vs polls reprices Brazil rates, FX, and agri/energy policy into the Oct 25 runoff (just outside this window).
events.what_to_watch: Endorsement flow and prediction-market odds already ~80%+ Flávio; soy/oil/mining policy signals.

events.title: Korea September CPI 2.9% with chip-price passthrough
events.why_it_matters: Inflation re-accelerated toward 3% as semiconductor prices lift durables — the domestic cost of the AI-memory boom.
events.what_to_watch: BoK commentary that October may stay ~3% if Middle East energy stays high.

events.title: September FOMC minutes (Warsh-era 25 bp hike)
events.why_it_matters: Minutes of the Sept 15–16 hike to 3.75–4.00% land after a labor miss that crushed October hike odds to ~20%; tone vs subsequent data is the trade.
events.what_to_watch: How many wanted another hike, inflation-persistence language, and whether 'no urgency' is already in the room.

events.title: China onshore markets reopen after Golden Week
events.why_it_matters: A-shares/Stock Connect return after a week of Hormuz, NFP, and holiday-spend news that traded only offshore.
events.what_to_watch: CNY, property developers, and consumer names vs holiday volume/spend split; gap vs HK.

events.title: Graham Act clock: Oct 8 justification, Oct 18 determinations
events.why_it_matters: Statute requires USTR justification ≥10 days before secondary tariffs and presidential Russia/third-country determinations by ~Oct 18 — stacking up to 100% on top of Section 301, likely aimed at China/India/Turkey.
events.what_to_watch: Covered-country list, waiver language, and whether China is named despite the Jan 10 truce.

events.title: PepsiCo Q3 2026 earnings (staples/pricing kickoff)
events.why_it_matters: First mega-cap staples print of the season tests elasticities under $100 oil and still-high food-at-home prices.
events.what_to_watch: Volume vs price mix, guidance, and any consumer-trade-down language that previews retail sales.

events.title: Delta Air Lines Q3 2026 earnings (jet-fuel stress test)
events.why_it_matters: Bellwether airline vs Brent >$100; Q3 plan assumed jet fuel far below wartime diesel/jet spikes.
events.what_to_watch: Unit-cost guide, capacity cuts, and whether demand still covers $100+ oil.

events.title: US bank Q3 cluster (JPM/GS/WFC/C Oct 13; BAC/MS Oct 14)
events.why_it_matters: NII, credit, and capital-markets prints after a labor miss and a still-inverted/war-premium curve set the financials tone for earnings season.
events.what_to_watch: Consumer charge-offs, reserve builds, trading revenue, and any recession language vs still-resilient services PMI.

events.title: UnitedHealth Q3 2026 earnings / Medicare Advantage margins
events.why_it_matters: Sector bellwether after a Q2 beat and 2027 MA footprint cuts (~390k members); medical-cost trend is the healthcare tape.
events.what_to_watch: MCR, MA margin (>3% FY guide), and any 2027 benefit-design/attrition update.

events.title: SEMICON West 2026 (San Francisco)
events.why_it_matters: Industry gathering as the sector crosses a $1tn revenue narrative; capex/tool commentary will be read against ASML/TSMC the same week.
events.what_to_watch: HBM/advanced-packaging tool demand, China-export-control chatter, and any 2027 capex cuts.

events.title: September CPI (consensus: hot headline, cooler core)
events.why_it_matters: Market expects ~+0.5–0.6% m/m headline (gasoline) and ~+0.2% core; a hot core would revive December hike odds after NFP killed October.
events.what_to_watch: Core/supercore vs energy; Kalshi already ~60% on >+0.5% headline m/m.

events.title: ASML Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: The lithography bottleneck print is the cleanest read on 2027 WFE/AI capex before TSMC the next morning.
events.what_to_watch: Gross bookings, China mix, High-NA commentary, and 2027 guide vs memory tightness.

events.title: September PPI and advance retail sales
events.why_it_matters: PPI (~+0.5% m/m expected) is the pipeline into CPI/PCE; retail sales test whether $100 oil is already destroying goods demand after the NFP miss.
events.what_to_watch: Control-group sales (GDP) and core PPI ex-food/energy vs gasoline passthrough.

events.title: TSMC Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Foundry bellwether for AI GPUs/HBM packaging; print lands into SEMICON week and Taiwan gray-zone noise.
events.what_to_watch: CoWoS/advanced-packaging capacity, 2026–27 capex, and any export-control or power/shipping comments.

events.title: Eurozone September HICP final
events.why_it_matters: Confirms or revises the 3.8% flash that already challenged the ECB's measured hold into Oct 29.
events.what_to_watch: Country mix and services; a revision higher would lift December hike odds even if Oct 29 is a hold.

events.title: CIT Section 301 supplemental briefs due
events.why_it_matters: Judges asked which 301 subsection USTR used and whether standing covers all 60 economies — the last written round before a ruling that could vacate global duties.
events.what_to_watch: Government's statutory theory and any hint the panel is leaning toward vacatur vs remand.

events.title: Europe aviation/transport strikes (IT/FR/BE cluster)
events.why_it_matters: Air Corsica, Italian flight/airport, Belgian ATC, and French flight-crew notices stack into peak autumn travel — a local traffic/airline cost overlay, not a macro shock.
events.what_to_watch: Cancellation rates and whether French Oct 17–21 action spreads to hubs.

events.title: US September housing starts and permits
events.why_it_matters: Last hard US housing print in this window after August starts at 1.275m; rates-plus-oil affordability is the risk to 2027 residential.
events.what_to_watch: Single-family permits vs multifamily; any weather/heat distortion in the West.

top_risks: Hormuz/Iran escalation (third carrier, more tanker strikes) into US midterms — regime-level oil and inflation shock
Graham Act Oct 8/18 secondary-tariff list naming China/India despite the Jan 10 truce — stacked duties on top of Section 301
Hot September core CPI (Oct 14) reopening December FOMC hike odds after NFP killed October
CIT vacatur path on global forced-labor Section 301 — binary for import costs and refunds
Oil-led demand destruction: NFP +29k already showed hiring freeze; retail sales/Delta test goods and travel
top_opportunities: Soft core CPI + labor miss = October pause (~80% hold) and duration/risk-on if headline oil spike is looked through
AI-memory/WFE confirmation: Micron tightness + ASML/TSMC/SEMICON week
US–China truce to Jan 10 and $60bn non-sensitive lists remove the near-term tariff cliff
China reopen Oct 8 if Golden Week volume converts into better-than-feared spend and PMI follow-through
Bank/UNH prints if credit and MA margins hold, capping the growth-scare tail
summary: The tape remains a two-factor regime: a live US–Iran war with Hormuz restricted and Brent near $100–102, versus a labor-market miss (+29k) that crushed October FOMC hike odds to ~20% with minutes due Oct 7. Policy is two-sided — a US–China truce to Jan 10 and $60bn relief lists cut the near-term China tariff cliff, while the Graham Act's Oct 8/18 secondary-tariff clock and the CIT challenge to global Section 301 keep trade risk binary. Q3 earnings open with PepsiCo then banks/UNH/ASML/TSMC against an AI-memory boom Micron has already validated; CPI/PPI/retail next week decide whether $100 oil is a tax or a growth break.
